transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-21
Start time: 17:30 UTC
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees: Noah (CEO), Isabel (Head of Product), Tom (CTO), Lena (VP Eng), Marcus (VP Sales), Sofia (Head Research), Emily (Head People) + all-hands.

Summary:
Noah opened with Q3 results, shortfall vs plan in a couple of enterprise renewals but strong demand from mid-market. Product walked through Dedicated autoscale, Private rollout milestones, and Console observability features. CTO reviewed incident and reliability improvements; security gave an update on SOC 2 and KMS integrations. Lots of Q&A about latency/cost tradeoffs and Dedicated capacity pricing. Ended with hiring goals and concrete next steps.

Topics covered (auto): Q3 KPIs, Product roadmap, Reliability & incidents, Security/compliance, Hiring & Org.

Action items (read out in meeting): see metadata list above.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Noah: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this tight, we've got about an hour. Quick pulse, Q3 shipped a lot, um, good momentum in the mid-market flows but a couple of enterprise renewals slipped, we'll dig in.
[00:22] Audience chatter / applause / muted lines.
[00:30] Noah: Quick numbers — ARR growth this quarter 16% sequential, CAC is steady, churn ticked up +0.8% vs last q, most of that tied to two accounts on dedicated renewals. Marcus you want to add?
[00:44] Marcus: Yeah thanks Noah, quick color — the two renewal deals had procurement timing and legal scoping, and one had a data residency ask that pushed timeline. We're following up with a dedicated proposal and legal addendum.
[00:58] Noah: Cool, product — Isabel?
[01:05] Isabel: Hi all, product highlights, first the Dedicated autoscale beta rolled to three customers, early signals show 12-18% cost reduction on steady-state when they use our batching + cache settings. Note: some of the telemetry was noisy — we improved logs in Console so SEs can see token-level cost.
[01:30] Isabel: Private deployments — we've completed the VPC connector and internal QA for the on-prem installer, early partner test next week. Also we're working on an optional HSM/KMS flow for key management, still gated by a couple of infra changes.
[01:52] Tom: On the KMS piece, quick note — integration needs key rotation logic in the runtime, and there were a few alignment tasks with our ops team. We're targeting L0 support in October. There was a question about latency overhead for KMS calls — we added async caching to reduce p99 impact.
[02:10] Lena: On infra — we shipped a kernel selection improvement that cuts single-request p50 by ~8% on Ampere, and we landed a KV cache compaction tweak, although the transcriber might read that as KV cash.
[02:28] Sofia: Research update — we've been evaluating smaller decoder-only models for rerank workloads, and the quality vs cost tradeoffs look promising; will share evals in the research channel. Also some experiments on quant profiles that seem stable.
[02:45] Audience: Uh-huh, applause.
[03:00] Noah: Reliability — Tom can you walk through the incident on 9/12?
[03:06] Tom: Yeah, short version, the 9/12 incident was a cascading routing misconfiguration combined with a bug in the continuous batching logic; some clients saw elevated latency and timeouts for about 37 minutes. Root cause: a config mismatch during a rollout where the router sent some traffic to an older model variant that didn't have the new KV cache handling. We've changed the rollout gating and added an automated check to ensure model-variant compat compatibility, and a canary step now verifies end-to-end request flows.
[03:35] Tom: Postmortem is being drafted, we'll publish a condensed version to the company by 2026-09-23.
[03:45] Isabel: From product side we also added a fallback policy that will route to a lower-cost instance instead of failing, so apps see graceful degradation not hard errors.
[03:59] Marcus: Sales note — we need a one-pager explaining the degradation/fallback guarantees for enterprise RFPs, I've got a template but will need engineering sign-off.
[04:12] Noah: Security — Sofia can give a short update on SOC 2 and audits.
[04:17] Sofia: Short update: we're on track for SOC 2 type II by end of Q4; auditor prep is underway. We've remediated 5 of the 8 medium items. KMS/HSM work is in parallel, and we've started a compliance checklist for Private on-prem customers that includes audit logs, SAML SSO, and RBAC.
[04:40] Audience question: Any data residency specifics for EU customers?
[04:47] Lena: We're adding region pinning and separate EU-backed storage options in our private control plane; we'll expose region labels in the Console UI.
[04:56] Marcus: Also legal is working on standard addendums for EU data residency.
[05:05] Noah: Product demos — Isabel quick demo of Console observability and new trace hooks?
[05:12] Isabel: Sure, quick walk-through — Console now shows per-route token-level cost, per-model latency histograms, and a new traces tab that links to request payload previews (with PII redaction by default). There are still a few UI polish items but the core telemetry is live.
[05:37] Isabel: We also put up a new Optimize suggestion engine that flags batch config changes and suggests quant profiles; it's early but SEs can opt-in per account.
[05:50] Audience murmur — questions in chat about opt-in and rollout.
[06:01] Q&A segment (mixed speakers)
[06:05] Employee A: Are we still recommending hosted vs dedicated for high-throughput mapping workloads?
[06:11] Isabel: Depends — hosted is fastest to start and cheaper at low volumes, Dedicated is recommended for predictable throughput and tight latency SLOs; we now have autoscale to make Dedicated more flexible for spikey traffic. The tradeoff is cost commitment vs operational control.
[06:33] Employee B: How about private/on-prem for regulated customers — timeline?
[06:36] Tom: Private GA for VPC connectors next month, on-prem installer is in partner testing, target general availability mid-Oct.
[06:45] Employee C: Will the KMS integration increase latency?
[06:48] Tom: We built async caching so cold KMS lookups are rare; there is a small p99 tail but we've mitigations and will document best practices.
[06:58] Employee D: Any change to pricing for Dedicated?
[07:02] Marcus: No across-the-board change — we're adding a burst capacity add-on SKU and clarifying commit tiers; pricing doc will be pushed to the AE playbook.
[07:15] Noah: Hiring & org — Emily?
[07:18] Emily: Hiring update: we added 14 hires this quarter, need to fill 8 roles — 3 infra/serving, 2 platform, 2 SE, 1 security. Referral bonuses adjusted, please refer. On org, we consolidated some product ownership around the Console and Optimize teams.
[07:40] Audience: applause.
[07:44] Audience Q: Any cross-functional OKR changes?
[07:47] Noah: We'll keep the overall OKRs, but shift a portion of Q4 capacity to reliability and security. Specific teams will get updated sub-okr doc by Friday.
[07:58] Misc small notes & kudos: shoutouts to infra for kernel selection work, to SEs for new onboarding templates, to research for evals.
[08:14] Noah: Closing — quick recap: product to share Dedicated autoscale FAQ, security to share SOC 2 roadmap, engineering to publish postmortem summary, sales to update playbook. Action items in the notes. Thanks everyone.
[08:30] Meeting ends, muted rooms and informal chat continues.

Note: transcript contains minor transcription errors and a couple of places where product names were misrecognized (e.g., "KV cash" for KV cache, "Redwood Infrence" in some auto-captions). Links referenced in meeting: internal deck: /docs/q3-company-deck-2026 (shared on slack), postmortem draft: /docs/incidents/2026-09-12-routing-postmortem (to be published), product timeline: /wiki/product/private-rollout.
